DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Title: Experience
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Mode.Split.Label: Split a total
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Mode.Split.Hint: One figure for the whole party, divided evenly — the book's own way (Player's Book p25)
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Mode.Each.Label: Per character
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Mode.Each.Hint: Type what each character earned, and let the window do the modifiers
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Total.Label: Party XP
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Total.Note.One: Divided evenly between the {count} counted below, then that character's own modifier.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Total.Note.Other: Divided evenly between the {count} counted below, then each character's own modifier.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Total.Reckon: Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or click away to reckon it.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Each.Hint: Type what each one earned in the Earned column. The share percentage and the Prime Ability modifier are still reckoned from it — this only skips the dividing.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Remainder.Label: {n} left over
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Remainder.Hint: What the division could not place, plus anything you took off a row by hand. The book does not say who gets the odd point, so nobody does until you say so.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Overspent.Label: {n} over the total
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Overspent.Hint: The shares below add up to more than the party earned, because a row was raised by hand. Nothing stops you — it is only worth knowing.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Forfeited.Label: {n} forfeited
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Forfeited.Hint: What a share percentage below 100 takes off the shares below. This is not left over for somebody else — a retainer earns half and the other half is simply not earned (Player's Book p25).
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.Include.Hint: Counted when the total is divided. Untick for anyone who was not there.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.Share.Hint: This character's share is set to {pct}% on the sheet — at 50 that is the book's rule for an adventurer retainer (Player's Book p25).
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.Percent.Hint: No Class to read it from, so this is the XP bonus field on the sheet. Typing here writes it there — set it once and it stays.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.LevelUp.Label: May level
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.LevelUp.Hint: Passes {next} XP, the threshold on the attribute sheet. Taking the Level is a separate step on the sheet — it costs time and coins.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.Capped.Label: capped, {lost} lost
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.Capped.Hint: The house cap stops a character at the threshold two Levels above them ({at} XP). {lost} XP had nowhere to go and were not credited.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Row.Reset.Hint: Put this row back on the even share
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Empty: No party characters this module can read. XP is kept by the game system, so a character needs Ability Scores before it can be credited any.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Clear.Label: Clear
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Clear.Hint: Empty every field and count everyone again
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Prime.FromClass: {class}: Prime {abilities}. The lowest score decides it — {lowest}.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Prime.ByHand: {class}, but the modifier was set by hand on the attribute sheet and that is what counts here.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Prime.UnknownClass: "{class}" is not a Class this module knows, so the modifier comes from the XP bonus field on the sheet.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Prime.NoClass: No Class on the sheet, so the modifier comes from the XP bonus field.
DOLMENWOOD.Xp.Confirm.NoUndo: Their XP totals are written straight to the sheet. There is no undo.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.Title: Trash
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.PlayerHint: These are the items you deleted. Ask your GM to put one back.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.Row.Delete.Hint: Throw this one away for good, and leave the rest of the bin alone
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.Restore.Failed: That item could not be restored — nowhere to put it.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.Restore.Fallback: Restored to {zone} — the zone it came from is gone or full.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.Discard.Title: Throw Away
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.Discard.Hint: It cannot be restored afterwards. The rest of the bin is untouched.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.EmptyActor.Title: Empty Trash
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.EmptyActor.Body.One: Throw away {count} deleted item from {name}'s trash? This cannot be undone.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.EmptyActor.Body.Other: Throw away {count} deleted items from {name}'s trash? This cannot be undone.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.EmptyAll.Label: Empty all
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.EmptyAll.Title: Empty All Trash
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.EmptyAll.Body.One: Throw away {count} deleted item across {where}? This cannot be undone.
DOLMENWOOD.Trash.EmptyAll.Body.Other: Throw away {count} deleted items across {where}? This cannot be undone.

DOLMENWOOD.Market.Dialog.OwnStock.Hint: Nothing from the catalogue, only what you put on this stall's shelf yourself. The categories below are then ignored.
DOLMENWOOD.Market.Dialog.Categories.Hint: Leave every box unticked to sell the whole catalogue. Treasures are never on a shelf by category — put one there with From Catalogue inside the shop.

DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Name.Hint: Name this inn — leave empty for none
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.QualityFixed.Hint: Set when this inn was placed
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Release.Open.Label: Open to the party

DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Release.Closed.Hint: Only you can reach this inn. Name it and set its quality first, then open it: the party is told in chat and the doors appear on their toolbar and day bar.
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.NewDay.Label: New day
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.NewDay.Hint: Start a new in-game day: clears this list and re-rolls every inn's menu
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Section.Quality.Hint: This section differs from the house quality

DOLMENWOOD.Inn.NobodyElse: There is nobody else to buy for.

This inn has its own edited tables. Changing the quality rebuilds every section from the book and discards those edits.

DOLMENWOOD.Inn.TakeAway.SubContainer: {portions} portions for the price of {price} — {cost}, {weight} wt
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Name.Label: Name
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Group.Label: Group
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Group.Note: (decides which daily draw it belongs to)
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Tag.Label: Small label
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Unit.Label: Price suffix
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Container.Label: Sold to take away as
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Container.Hint: “Automatic” follows the house's switch and the type above — cask for beer and cider, bottle for wine, spirits and specialities, nothing for tea. A fixed choice overrides the house switch in both directions.
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Grants.Label: Hands over
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Grants.Hint: Normally nothing — what is bought at an inn is consumed on the spot. Pick a catalog item and this line becomes a purchase of goods instead: it goes into a pack, with a target zone and an amount, and it stacks with the same item bought in a shop. This is how rations work.
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Fixed.Label: Always available
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.Line.Fixed.Hint: The house's own brew or signature dish — never part of the daily roll.
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.SectionDialog.Title: Section settings
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.SectionDialog.Quality.Hin: Changing this rebuilds the section from the book — the three levels are separate tables.
Sells drink by the bottle and cask
The house default. A single drink can still be set to its own answer, which wins either way — so a house that sells nothing to take away can still let its own brew out by the cask.
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.SectionDialog.Draw.Legend: How many are served each day
DOLMENWOOD.Inn.SectionDialog.Draw.Hint: Leave a pair empty to serve every line in that group.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Name.Hint: Name this shop — leave empty for none

DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Shelf.Own.Hint: This shop sells only what you have put on its shelf. Click to sell the whole catalogue instead.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Shelf.Catalogue.Label: Catalogue
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Shelf.Catalogue.Hint: This shop sells the whole catalogue. Click to keep it to its own shelf — which is what makes it a shop rather than a warehouse.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Release.Open.Label: Open to the party
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Release.Open.Hint: The party can reach this shop from the toolbar, the day bar and their own inventory. Click to shut it again — anyone with it open will have it taken away.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Release.Closed.Label: Closed
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Release.Closed.Hint: Only you can reach this shop. Name it and stock it first, then open it: the party is told in chat and the doors on their bar light up.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Coins.Label: Coins:
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Coins.Hint: Every coin {name} is carrying, wherever it is stowed — belt, pack, cart and all
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Affordable.Label: Affordable

DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellMode.Label: Sell

DOLMENWOOD.Shop.AddToShop.HintGeneral: Add goods or a service that stay in the general shop permanently
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.FromCatalogue.Label: From Catalogue
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.FromCatalogue.Hint: Put catalogue items on this shelf by hand — including the treasures that are never on sale by default
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.AddService.Label: Add a Service
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.AddService.Hint: Put a service on this shelf: the Player's Book specialists, and whatever you have written yourself
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.NewVisit.Label: New visit
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.NewVisit.Hint: Roll again for everything this shop stocks on a chance. Visit {n}.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.Note: {shop} pays {pct}% of what a thing is worth — reckoned on its own value, not on this shop's asking price.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.OnlyTrade: It takes only what it deals in: {list}.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.NoZones: Anything that carries a zone of its own (a backpack, a cart) is not listed: selling one would have to decide what happens to everything inside it.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.Fill.Label: {used} of {capacity}
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.Fill.Hint: The shop pays for what is in it, not for the empty container
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.InHand.Label: {n} in hand
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.All.Label: all: {cost}
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.Button.Label: Sell
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.SellView.Empty: {name} has nothing this shop would take.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Badge.Service.Hint: A service: nothing is added to the inventory
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Badge.Out.Label: out this visit
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Badge.Out.Hint: Stocked on a {n}-in-6 chance, and not in this visit. Players do not see this row at all.
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Badge.Chance.Label: {n}-in-6
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Badge.Chance.Hint: Stocked on a {n}-in-6 chance, rolled once per visit
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Buy.Label: Buy
DOLMENWOOD.Shop.Pay.Label: Pay

DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.NewDay: Move on to the next in-game day
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Doing: What the party is doing today
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Tp.SpendPart: Spend a Travel Point — {part} of the day
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.MySheet: My attributes, saves, skills and traits
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.ResetDay: Clear today's ticks and spent Travel Points without moving the day on
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.HideBar: Hide the bar entirely (bring it back from the toolbar)
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.Ate.Label: Ate
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.Ate.Hint: Characters who have eaten today. Everyone needs a ration a day — hunger costs -1 Attack from day one and 1 Constitution a day from day seven (Player's Book p153).
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.Ate.Row: Eating a ration from the inventory or a meal at an inn ticks this by itself
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.Slept.Label: Slept well
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.Slept.Hint: Characters who got a GOOD night's rest. Anything less leaves them exhausted until they do (Player's Book p159).
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.Slept.Row: A GOOD night's rest, not merely lying down: easy conditions are automatic, moderate and difficult ones need a Constitution Check, impossible ones fail outright (Player's Book p159). Paying for lodging at an inn ticks this by itself.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.NoRest.Label: No rest
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.NoRest.Row: Travel days since this character last rested. The counter rises on every day the party spends a Travel Point, and clears on a day it spends none and this character sleeps well. A week is six travel days and one of rest, so the seventh travel day without one costs -1 to Attack and Damage Rolls until it is taken (Player's Book p157). A forced march owes its rest day at once. Click to clear both by hand.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Panel.ForcedMarches: Forced marches since the last rest day
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.TickByHand: Tick off by hand, without rolling
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.TakeRollBack: Take this roll back so it can be made again
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.ShowWeather: Show the weather on this map
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.OpenDuty: Open this duty to the players
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.OpenStep: Open this step to the players
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Group.TickAll: Tick every step of this group
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Group.ClearAll: Clear every step of this group
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Moved.Label: Party moved
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Moved.Crossed: A token has crossed a hex boundary on {scene} since this was last set.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Moved.Uncalibrated: Reading the hex off the token is switched on, but this map has not been calibrated: stand the token in a hex you know, type it in the box and press the crosshairs. Until then, check the terrain and the way by hand.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Moved.ByHand: Check the terrain and the way — the module cannot read them off the map.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Moved.Confirm: Change one of them, or click to say it is still right.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.TerrainHint: {label} ({band}): {blurb}. {chance}-in-6 to lose the way or to meet something; {cost} Travel Points to enter or search a hex. {travel}
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.SettlementNone: Which of the twelve settlements the Campaign Book details the party is in. Only the Settlement tab's encounter rolls use it — everywhere else it is ignored, and a hamlet the book does not cover has no table.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.SettlementHint: {settlement}. Its own d6 encounter tables, day and night, are what the Settlement tab rolls on. It does not replace the region: the party is still in {region} the moment they leave.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.RegionAquatic: Aquatic is the column for a day spent on a river or a lake, not a place on the map. Chosen, an encounter is rolled straight off it, as the Campaign Book directs (p114).
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.RegionHint: {region} — which regional encounter table this hex reads (Campaign Book p115). A region is a dozen hexes across, so this changes far less often than the terrain does.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.LostNone: No chance of losing the way
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.HexHint: {hex}, {name}. {terrain}, {region}, {lost} to lose the way. Described in the Campaign Book on p{page}.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Ctx.HexEmpty: The hex the party is standing in. Type it and the terrain, the region and the lost chance follow from the Campaign Book — including anything that grows here which the foraging tables do not know about. A hex the book does not detail is still kept; set the terrain by hand.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Calibrate.Label: Calibrate
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Calibrate.Follows: Moving a token sets the hex by itself.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Calibrate.SwitchOn: Switch on “Read the hex off the party's token” in the module settings to use it.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Calibrate.Afresh: Press again to measure it afresh, starting from the first point.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Calibrate.Point1: Point 1 is {hex}. Now put the token one hex to the left or right — the next column along — type that hex in the box and press again. Two points are needed because the columns are staggered by half a hex, and which way they lean is the thing a single measurement cannot say.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Calibrate.Hint: Calibrate this map. Stand the party's token in a hex you know, select it, type that hex in the box and press this; then do the same one column to the left or right. From then on the module reads the hex off any position on this map.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Weather.Unrolled: The day's weather has not been rolled yet.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Budget.NoConvoy: No party convoy to read a Speed from, so there is no allowance to count against.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Budget.Spent: {used} of the day's {total} Travel Points spent. The allowance is fixed when the day starts — the party's Speed divided by 5, and half as many again on a forced march (Player's Book p156) — so it does not shift under the march when a load or a ration changes. Unspent points are lost at nightfall.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Budget.PerPoint: Twelve hours on the road split {marched} ways: each point spent is {each}, and the world clock moves with it.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Budget.PerPointForced: Sixteen hours on the road split {marched} ways: each point spent is {each}, and the world clock moves with it.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Budget.Stopped: That leaves nothing at all — the party can only progress by forced marching today.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Budget.Over: More has been spent than the allowance now allows: the extra points were walked under a forced march that has since been called off.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Refresh.Stale: The party would be worth {derived} Travel Points as they stand now, against the {started} this day was started with. Click to adopt {derived} — the points already spent stay spent.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Refresh.Hint: Re-read the day's allowance from the party as they stand now. It is fixed at the start of the day on purpose, so this is only for when their circumstances really have changed.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Forced.On: Forced march: {from} Travel Points become {to}, at the price of a 16 hour day. Every character who marches owes a full rest day afterwards or is exhausted, -1 to Attack and Damage; marching again before that rest adds another -1 (Player's Book p156). Click to call it off.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Forced.Off: Normal travel. Click to declare a forced march: half as many Travel Points again, a 16 hour day, and a rest day owed afterwards (Player's Book p156).
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.NoCharacter: No character assigned to you, and no token selected.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.InnShut: The inn is not open yet.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.ShopShut: The shop is not open yet.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.NoActor: No actor found. Assign a character to your user first.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.NoMap: There is no map in view to show the weather on.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.Point1: Point 1 of 2: {hex} on {scene}. Now move the token one hex to the left or right — into the next column — type that hex in the box, and press the crosshairs again. The second measurement is what tells the module which way the columns are staggered.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.CalibratedShift: {scene} is calibrated: {a} and {b}, with the columns half a hex apart.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.Follows: Move the token and the hex on the bar follows.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Msg.FxOff: {scene} no longer shows the day's weather, and what was on it has been taken down.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.NewDayDialog.Title: New Day
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.NewDayDialog.Ask: Move on to the next day?
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.NewDayDialog.Hint: Every inn re-rolls its menu, the duty list starts fresh, and each character's hunger and rest clocks move on — anyone who did not eat today gains a day of hunger.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Fx.Nothing: Today there is nothing to draw.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Fx.Stop: Click to stop drawing it here.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Fx.Off: Draw the day's weather on {here}. Only the maps switched on here are ever touched, and weather you set through FXMaster yourself is left alone.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Key.ScopeOwn: Each of them may roll it once today, for their own character.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Key.ScopeParty: One of them may roll it for the party, once.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Key.Closed: Closed. Turn the key when this part of the day is happening, and the players get the die for it.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Roll.Secret: Roll it. Real dice, and the result is whispered to the Referee alone.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Roll.Open: Roll it. Real dice, and the result is announced to the table.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Group.Title: Duties
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Deny.SettingOff: The table has not switched the players' own rolls on.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Deny.NotOpen: The Referee has not opened this one yet.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Deny.NoCharacter: No character of yours to roll it for.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Deny.AlreadyOwn: Already done today. It comes back with the next day.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Deny.Leader: The party leader rolls this one.
DOLMENWOOD.DayBar.Deny.AlreadyParty: Somebody has already done this today.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Weather.Label: Weather
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Weather.Hint: Roll the day's weather on the Campaign Book tables — the Travel and the Settlement procedure both open with it. Fog and blizzards also raise the chance of getting lost, and the season decides how hard it is to sleep out.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Healing.Label: Healing
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Healing.Hint: Those who got a good night's rest heal 1 HP. A full day of rest in a settlement heals 1d3 instead, but precludes anything more strenuous than an inn chair.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.PrepareSpells.Label: Prepare spells
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.PrepareSpells.Hint: Spell-casters memorise or pray for the day's spells. A character who failed to get a good night's rest has a 1-in-6 chance of losing each spell they try to prepare.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Lost.Label: Getting lost
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Lost.Hint: One roll per travel day, made at the start of it. 1-in-6 in light terrain and on tracks, 2-in-6 moderate, 3-in-6 difficult; +1 in fog, +2 in darkness. No chance at all on a road.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.EncounterDay.Label: Encounter (day)
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.EncounterDay.Hint: One daytime wandering-monster check. In the wilds the chance is the terrain's (1/2/3-in-6); in a settlement it is 2-in-6 while the party is out and about.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Forage.Label: Finding food
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Forage.Hint: Optional — ONE Survival Check per travelling group per day, on the best Skill Target among them (Player's Book p152). Splitting up allows a check each, at the cost of a separate getting-lost and wandering-monster check per group. Foraging yields 1d6 fresh rations, 1d4 in winter and 1d8 in autumn; a whole day given over to it grants +2.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Campsite.Label: Campsite
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Campsite.Hint: At least one character stays back to clear ground, pitch tents, and dig a fire pit.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Firewood.Label: Firewood
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Firewood.Hint: Each character fetching wood collects enough for 1d6 hours of fire. Damp -1, snow -2, heavy rain -4.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Water.Label: Water
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Water.Hint: Refill waterskins. Easy almost everywhere in Dolmenwood — but a character without water loses 3 Constitution a day.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Fire.Label: Fire
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Fire.Hint: Automatic given a tinder box and wood; 4-in-6 or worse in troublesome conditions. A campfire eases the sleep difficulty for everyone who has bedding, and for nobody who has not.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Cooking.Label: Cooking
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Cooking.Hint: Optional Wisdom Check. Success gives everyone +1 on the Constitution Check to rest; a natural 1 means Save Versus Doom or the ingredients are ruined.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Entertainment.Label: Camaraderie
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Entertainment.Hint: Optional Charisma Check. Success gives everyone +1 on the Constitution Check to rest; a natural 1 means Save Versus Doom or -1 instead.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Watches.Label: Watches
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Watches.Hint: Usually four characters taking 2 hour watches across 8 hours. Under 6 hours of sleep is not a good night's rest, and a broken night makes spell preparation harder. Rolling it uses the optional falling-asleep-on-watch rule.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.EncounterNight.Label: Encounter (night)
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.EncounterNight.Hint: One nighttime wandering-monster check — the terrain's chance while camping, 1-in-6 in a settlement if the party is active. Sleeping characters are automatically surprised.
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Sleep.Label: Sleep
DOLMENWOOD.Duty.Sleep.Hint: Bedding down. Fire, bedding and the season set the difficulty; an easy night is automatic, a moderate or difficult one is a Constitution Check, and an impossible one fails outright. Failing it means exhaustion until they do sleep well.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Winter.Label: Winter
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Winter.Hint: Winter's hold is light since the Cold Prince was vanquished — the waters seldom freeze, and snow rarely piles deep. Foraging yields only 1d4.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Spring.Label: Spring
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Spring.Hint: Sunny and clement. Dolmenwood is widely held to be at its most beautiful.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Summer.Label: Summer
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Summer.Hint: Hot, humid, and abuzz with insects. Sprite season — Lillipythe is awash with them.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Autumn.Label: Autumn
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Autumn.Hint: The best foraging of the year: 1d8 rations rather than the usual 1d6.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Hitching.Label: Hitching
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Hitching.Hint: Unseason. The trees drip with dew, balmy mists fill the woods, and the fey moon shines beside the true one. Has a weather table of its own; falls in winter, so foraging yields 1d4.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Colliggwyld.Label: Colliggwyld
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Colliggwyld.Hint: Unseason. Giant fungi bloom throughout the Wood, and foraged fungi are found in DOUBLE quantity. Uses the spring weather table.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Chame.Label: Chame
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Chame.Hint: Unseason. Serpents fill the wood. Any encounter has a 2-in-6 chance of being snakes or wyrms instead. Uses the summer weather table.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Vague.Label: Vague
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Vague.Months: unseason — 1d6 days in Lymewald or Haggryme
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Season.Vague.Hint: Unseason. A sinister fog rolls from the earth and the dead rise with it. Any encounter has a 2-in-6 chance of being undead. Has a weather table of its own; falls in winter, so foraging yields 1d4.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Band.Light.Label: Light
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Band.Moderate.Label: Moderate
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Band.Moderate.Travel: Mounts must be led; no vehicles.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Band.Difficult.Label: Difficult
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.Farmland.Label: Farmland
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.Hills.Label: Hills
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.Meadow.Label: Meadow
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.OpenForest.Label: Open forest
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.Bog.Label: Bog
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.HillyForest.Label: Hilly forest
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.BoggyForest.Label: Boggy forest
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Terrain.Swamp.Label: Swamp
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Way.Road.Label: Road
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Way.Road.Hint: An actively maintained road. Travel is quick and there is no chance of getting lost at all — the roll is made only when the party leaves it.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Way.Track.Label: Track
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Way.Track.Hint: A smaller path, seldom frequented and sporadically maintained. Travel is quick, with a small risk of losing the way.
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Way.Wild.Label: Wild
DOLMENWOOD.Ctx.Way.Wild.Hint: Off roads and tracks. Speed and the chance of getting lost both come from the terrain.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Reason.WildFog: {chance}-in-6 travelling wild in {terrain} ({band} terrain), +1 for poor visibility (Campaign Book p112).
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Effect.Impeded.Label: Travel impeded
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Effect.Impeded.Hint: The party's daily Travel Points are reduced by 2. If that brings them to 0 or below, the party can only progress by forced marching.
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Effect.Visibility.Hin: Encounter distance is halved, and the chance of getting lost while travelling wild rises by 1-in-6.
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Effect.Wet.Label: Wet conditions
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Effect.Wet.Hint: Building a campfire is difficult. Gathering firewood yields less: -1 damp, -2 snow, -4 heavy rain.
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Borrowed: {season} has no weather table of its own — rolled on {table}.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.WeatherHint: Read off this morning's weather — {weather} — which the module scores as {penalty} to the roll. Change it if the Referee sees it differently.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.WeatherHintNone: Read off this morning's weather — {weather} — which the module scores as no penalty at all. Change it if the Referee sees it differently.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.NoWeather: The weather has not been rolled today, so nothing is assumed.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Reason.Road: No chance at all: the party is following a maintained road. The roll is made only when they leave it.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Reason.Track: 1-in-6 on a track. The Player's Book calls it "a small risk" without printing a figure, so this module uses the smallest one the Terrain Types table offers. Poor visibility adds nothing here: the Campaign Book raises the chance for travelling wild only.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R3: Lost in time. Travel is along the intended course, but 1d4+1 days pass.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R4: Accidentally stumble into a randomly selected fairy road (Fairy Roads, Campaign Book p26).
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R5: Move in circles, ending the day where it began.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R6: Travel 90° to the left of the intended course — two hex faces to the left, a hex having no 90°.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R8: Travel 45° to the left of the intended course — one hex face to the left, a hex having no 45°.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R10: Travel along the intended course, but uncertain paths cause all Travel Point costs to be doubled.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R12: Travel 45° to the right of the intended course — one hex face to the right, a hex having no 45°.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R14: Travel 90° to the right of the intended course — two hex faces to the right, a hex having no 90°.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R16: Move in circles, ending the day where it began.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R17: Knocked unconscious by flashing, coloured lights. Awaken 1d4 hours later in the hex of a randomly selected nodal stone (Ley Lines and Standing Stones, Campaign Book p18).
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Consequence.R18: Enveloped in a bewildering fog. Emerge at the end of the day in a randomly selected hex, at least 2 hexes from the original.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Card.NoRoll: No roll: the party is on a road.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Card.Secret: Off-course: the Campaign Book lets you keep this to yourself and let their map go wrong, or tell them the direction they are really walking. Either way they cannot correct it today.
DOLMENWOOD.Lost.Card.Hunter: A hunter in the party can find the path again on a 3-in-6 chance.
DOLMENWOOD.Settings.WeatherSound.Name: Play the day's weather
DOLMENWOOD.Settings.WeatherSound.Hint: Loops Simple Weather's own sound files for whatever the day was rolled as — rain under thunder under wind, together rather than one after another. A fair day plays nothing. This module keeps a playlist of its own, so Simple Weather's weather and this one never stop each other.
DOLMENWOOD.Settings.WeatherSoundVolume.H: How loud the weather is, as a percentage of the environment channel — so each listener's own ambient slider still governs it. Each kind of weather has a level of its own beneath this, set by ear: rain is louder than snow whatever you put here. At 50 every one of them plays at the figure it was tuned to; lower settings scale the whole weather down together.
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Audition.Title: Weather sound — audition
DOLMENWOOD.Weather.Audition.Hint: Every row that makes a sound, at the levels it would play at today. {sounding} of them; the other {silent} are fog, mist or a clear sky and are silent on purpose. Pressing one does not change the day.
DOLMENWOOD.Settings.ClockLapse.Name: Let the clock run on as the party travels
DOLMENWOOD.Settings.ClockLapse.Hint: How many seconds the world clock takes to walk forward when a move spends Travel Points, instead of jumping. Every clock at the table follows the same world time, so Smalltime and Simple Calendar sweep along with it. Set it to 0 for the old behaviour: the hours arrive at once. Handing a point back walks the clock the same way in reverse.
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Spells.Title: Preparing spells
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Spells.NoneYours: None of your spell-casters lost sleep last night — there is nothing for you to roll.
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Spells.Hint: These spell-casters failed to get a good night's rest, so each spell they try to memorise or pray for has a {chance}-in-6 chance of failing — the slot stays empty and unusable today. Only Classes that prepare spells are listed; the numbers are remembered on the characters, so this is asked properly only once.
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Spells.Rested: Everyone else in the party slept well and prepares their spells without rolling.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Title: Finding food in the wild
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Who.Hint: Who goes looking. The target follows whoever is picked — the best forager is the lowest number.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Check.Hint: 1d6 plus modifiers, meeting or exceeding the forager's own Survival target. A natural 1 always fails and a natural 6 always succeeds, whatever the modifiers.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Mod.Label: Situational modifier
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Store.Label: Rations go to
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Store.Hint: A fresh ration is 1 gear slot and 20 coins of weight (Player's Book p116, p149), so a good day's fishing is a real load — the party's own store is there for exactly that. Hunting stores nothing yet: its card carries a button for once the game is down.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.FullDay: A whole day given to it, travelling nowhere (+{bonus})
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Context.Hint: Hunting rolls against {terrain}, foraging against {season} — both from the bar's "where are we?" row.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Fish.Label: Fish
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Fish.Needs: A fishing rod and tackle, and a hex with a lake or river.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Fish.Hint: Roll 1d20 for the catch. Several of them are a hazard to land or to prepare, and a giant catfish is a combat encounter in its own right.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Forage.Label: Forage
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Forage.Hint: 1d6 decides fungi (1–3) or plants (4–6), then 1d20 for which. Some hexes list their own special finds, instead of or as well as these.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Hunt.Label: Hunt
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Hunt.Yield: By the quarry's Hit Points, once killed
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Hunt.Needs: The terrain decides what there is to stalk.
DOLMENWOOD.Food.Method.Hunt.Hint: Success only means the party has crept up on game. The kill is a normal combat encounter — the party has surprise and starts 1d4×30 feet away — and the rations come from what falls: 1 per HP small, 2 medium, 4 large.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Title: Rations from the kill
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.NoHolders: No party characters to carry it.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Intro: Fresh rations by the Hit Points of what fell — the book's own rate.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.IntroNamed: {beast}. Fresh rations by the Hit Points of what fell — the book's own rate.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.HitPoints.Label: Hit Points killed
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Book.Hint: The book gives one {beast} {hp} Hit Points, about {average} (Monster Book p{page}). Add up whichever of them actually fell.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Name.Label: Called
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Name.Hint: The meat goes into the pack under this name, not as "fresh rations" — so the players can note what eating it does. It weighs and feeds the same either way.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.NothingFell: Nothing fell, so nothing was butchered.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Holder.Label: Into the pack of
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Holder.Preset: Already chosen when the hunt was rolled. Change it if the haul is more than that pack can hold.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Count.One: {count} fresh ration — {count} slot, {weight} coins of weight.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Count.Other: {count} fresh rations — {count} slots, {weight} coins of weight.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Size.FromBook: Set from the stat block: the Monster Book calls a {beast} {size}.
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Size.Small.Label: Small — 1 ration per Hit Point
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Size.Medium.Label: Medium — 2 rations per Hit Point
DOLMENWOOD.Hunt.Size.Large.Label: Large — 4 rations per Hit Point
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Healing.Title: Waking up
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Healing.Sub: A good night's rest in the wild or a night in a settlement · {book}
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Healing.Foot: A full day of rest heals 1d3 instead, and is not this button's business — it precludes anything more strenuous than an inn chair.
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Passed.NoHp: no Hit Points on this sheet
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Spells.CardSub: {chance}-in-6 per spell, for a caster who failed to get a good night's rest · {book}
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Spells.Consequence: Those slots stay empty and unusable today.
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Spells.FreeSub: Everyone got a good night's rest, so no spell is at risk · {book}
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Warn.AllFull: Everyone rested is at full Hit Points
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Warn.NobodyRested: Nobody rested — no healing this morning
DOLMENWOOD.Morning.Warn.NoRollNeeded: Everyone slept well — no roll needed
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.NoParty: No party characters found. A character counts as party when a player owns it.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Title: Fetching firewood
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Hint: Each character who goes brings back enough wood for 1d6 hours of campfire, less whatever the weather costs. A night is {night} hours.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Empty: Nobody is carrying firewood. Light it anyway if the wood came from somewhere the module cannot see — nothing will leave the packs, and the Sleep Difficulty table will be rolled from its no-fire rows.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.OnFire.One: Wood on the fire. {count} hour in the packs, and a rest period is {night}. What is put on is burned whether the fire catches or not.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.OnFire.Other: Wood on the fire. {count} hours in the packs, and a rest period is {night}. What is put on is burned whether the fire catches or not.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Count.None: Nothing on the fire — the night is rolled cold.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Count.Under.One: {count} hour — under {minimum}, so not a night's fire at all.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Count.Under.Other: {count} hours — under {minimum}, so not a night's fire at all.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Count.Short.One: {count} hour — {short} short of the night, so −1 on the sleep check.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Count.Short.Other: {count} hours — {short} short of the night, so −1 on the sleep check.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Count.Full.One: {count} hour — enough for the whole night.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Wood.Count.Full.Other: {count} hours — enough for the whole night.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Fire.Title: Building a fire
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Fire.Hint: Given a tinder box and a stash of wood, fire building succeeds by itself. In troublesome circumstances the Referee may put a chance on it.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Fire.WetHint: Today's weather was wet, so the book's 4-in-6 is pre-picked.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Cooking.Label: Cooking
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Cooking.Success: An especially tasty dish. Everyone who eats it gains +1 on any Constitution Check to rest.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Cooking.Failure: Palatable, but not exemplary. No bonus to the night's rest.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Cooking.Doom: The meal is ruined and utterly inedible — burned, spilled — and the ingredients used are wasted.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Camaraderie.Suc: Spirits lift. Everyone gains +1 on any Constitution Check to rest.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Camaraderie.Fai: The attempt falls flat. No bonus to the night's rest.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Camaraderie.Doo: Ridicule and discord: -1 on any Constitution Check to rest.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.Hint: 1d6 plus the modifier, meeting or exceeding {target}. {success}
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Activity.DoomHint: Only ever rolled on a natural 1: {doom} The number follows the character where their sheet carries one — type one here for a character whose saves have not been filled in.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Eat.Title: Who eats?
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Eat.Hint.One: The pot holds {count} portion — one a head. Eating settles today's hunger.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Eat.Hint.Other: The pot holds {count} portions — one a head. Eating settles today's hunger.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Eat.Over: {ticked} named for {portions} portions — the last {hungry} go hungry.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Meal.Empty: The party is carrying nothing edible. Cook anyway if the ingredients came from somewhere the module cannot see — nothing will be taken from the packs.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Meal.Hint: Ingredients. One portion feeds one character. What is taken leaves the packs when the roll is made, whether the dish turns out well or not — who eats it is asked afterwards.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Meal.Count.One: {count} portion — enough for {fed} of the {party} in the party.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Meal.Count.Other: {count} portions — enough for {fed} of the {party} in the party.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Watch.Title: Watches through the night
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Watch.Hint: Tick who stands watch and drag the rows into the order they take them. The optional rule: a 1-in-10 chance of nodding off, 1-in-20 at Constitution 15 or higher, 1-in-6 at 6 or lower.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Watch.CountNone: Nobody on watch — everyone sleeps the night through.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Watch.CountShort: , under the {hours} hours a good night's rest takes.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Sleep.NotYours: None of these characters are yours to bed down.

DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Sleep.RousedHint: Tick it where the watcher shook the others awake, or the noise did it for them. Left unticked the night runs on — a wanderer who stops for a word with the watcher costs nobody their rest. Ticked, the night's rest ends there, and the earlier it happened the less anybody got.
DOLMENWOOD.Camp.Sleep.Card.Roused: The camp was roused in watch {watch}, and the night's rest ended there.

DOLMENWOOD.Block.Group.Label: Heading
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Group.Hint: Blocks are grouped under whatever heading you type. The module ships no class or spell lists on purpose — write what you play.
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Name.Label: Name
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Text.Label: What it says
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Value.Label: Lends this number to other rolls
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Value.Hint:
Optional, and only useful if something else should read it. Give this block a number and any other formula on the sheet can borrow it by name: write {slug} in another block's Added to the roll box and it will add this number.
So a trait called Keen Nose holding 2 lets a Search check be written as @b.keen-nose, and changing the 2 later changes every roll that leans on it. Leave it empty if nothing needs to refer to this block.
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Uses.Label: Uses per day
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Spell.Label: Is it a spell?
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Spell.No: No — a trait, an ability, a knack
DOLMENWOOD.Block.Spell.Hint: Only a spell gets the prepared tick on the sheet. The two kinds are kept apart because the books do: an arcane caster memorises from spell books that must be to hand and only from what they have written down (p78), while a holy caster prays for an hour and may choose any spell of their Rank (p100). The morning's 1-in-6 loss after a broken night falls on both alike.
